answer: Under the Cedar rule an identity self-declares value V, pays 2% of V per epoch as burn, and anyone may force-buy at V. Self-assessment is an honest signal: V too low and a rival seizes the account plus rewards; too high and tax drains it. A public lantern board lists all V, auditable. Validators enforce: two missed payments demote it to pending; forced-buys settle atomically. A sybil with n identities pays n taxes per epoch, each tax growing with locked rewards: marginal cost rises linearly in n. V prices future epochs and burns are irreversible: nothing is pre-farmable.
